Fire Mage Rotation in 

Fire Mage gameplay is simple with very few skills, but most of the difficulty of Fire comes down to execution. You will often be reacting based on whether one of your spells scores a Critical Strike, which grants Heating Up . This can be converted with Fire Blast into Hot Streak! for instant cast Pyroblast s. 

 
 

 
 Convert and Spend Hot Streak: Critical strikes generate Heating Up and Hot Streak! , spend these on Pyroblast (or Flamestrike in AoE). Use Fire Blast to convert Heating up into Hot Streak. 
 

 

 
 

 
 Combustion is Key: Combustion makes all spells guaranteed Critical Strikes, supercharging Hot Streak! generation. This spell can be cast while casting, so try to always activate it at the end of a cast. 
 

 

 
 
 
 Don't Waste Time: Sitting on capped Fire Blast charges, or using them when you already have Hot Streak! up is wasteful. Try to make full use of cooldowns and buffs. Always be casting. 
 

 

Fire Mage Starter Guide

 Best Fire Mage Opener

The optimal Fire Mage opener makes use of Firestarter and sets up your Combustion window with a "Double Pyroblast" . The idea is to have as many instant cast Pyroblast casts as possible. Activating Combustion while casting other spells allows us to fit more spells into the cooldown. After activating Combustion , proceed to the Single-Target or AoE Priority tab.

Pre-Combat Check

 Before any combat happens, it is important for Fire Mage to make sure the following are done. This applies to raids, dungeons, delves, or even open-world content.

 Fire Mage Major Cooldowns

Fire Mage only has one major cooldown ( Combustion ), but it has a huge impact on gameplay. Meteor is a minor cooldown, and is mostly used in tandem with Combustion .

 
 Combustion 

All spells Critically Strike during Combustion , making you a Hot Streak! machine gun. It has many interactions that either grant other buffs, increase proc chance, speed up cooldown recovery, or boost damage. Key takeaways are:
 
 Combustion can be cast while casting. Always cast a hard-cast into Combustion , but be sure to activate it before the cast completes. Viable spells are:

 Pyroblast or Flamestrike (AoE) with a Pyroclasm proc.

 Frostfire Bolt if Frostfire .

 Scorch if Sunfury .

 Fireball .
 

When playing Firestarter , Combustion should be delayed until the target reaches 90% health (Typically around 18 seconds).
If not playing Firestarter , Combustion should still be delayed on the pull (Around 8-10 seconds).
 
We do this to pre-stack buffs like Fired Up and because Fire Blast charges are plentiful.
 

After the opener, Combustion should generally be used on cooldown. Sometimes you will delay Combustion for better overlaps with AoE, Damage amps, or to avoid forced downtime. Plan ahead so you don't end up delaying and having it backfire, by costing you a use. 
 Fired Up is our new Apex talent. It has a chance to proc when you spend Hot Streak! .
 
 Combustion can be extended by Fired Up procs.

During Combustion , your first 3 Fired Up procs are almost guaranteed.
 

 Fiery Rush speeds up the Fire Blast cooldown during Combustion .
Critical Strike is not useless during Combustion . Burn It All and Slow Burn convert Crit into other effects. Unfortunately, this does not boost Critical Strike much.
When Combustion ends, Burnout causes all targets with an active Mastery: Ignite to take extra damage. This damage depends on the "size" of the Ignite.
 
To maximize Burnout in Single Target, Meteor should be used within 10 seconds of Combustion ending. This buff gets randomly extended, so shoot for <8 seconds remaining to give yourself some wiggle room.
 

For the Combustion window is longer, summons an Arcane Phoenix , and ends with Hyperthermia :

 
 Hyperthermia is a buff that allows you to rapidly fire Pyroblast or Flamestrike casts.

These casts are free, guaranteed to Crit, and ramp in damage.

You also gain a Haste buff from Ashes of Inspiration during this time. 
 

For the Combustion window is shorter and has no follow-up buffs. 

 Fire Mage Advanced Tips

The best thing you can do to improve your damage as a Fire Mage is to always be casting . Idle time in combat, caused by inactivity or poor movement, adds up and will greatly affect your damage. Mastering movement and keeping focus during combat is unequivocally the best way to raise your damage.

 
 Double Pyroblast and Finding your Rhythm

This guide has many mentions to "Double Pyroblast". When a Fireball (or other cast) completes, and is followed by an instant Pyroblast , both spells go off at the same time. If both Critically Strike, you will gain another Hot Streak! . Normally this is hard to predict, but Firestarter and Combustion make it guaranteed. This works because two spells were in flight, and two spells Crit. If two spells Crit at the same time, you skip Heating Up , straight to Hot Streak! . That is Double Pyroblast.

The beauty of Double Pyroblast is that it places the travel time of the spells during Global Cooldown, meaning that you won't lost time waiting for them to hit. There are many ways you can pull this off, but the key factors are:

 
You are guaranteed to Crit.

You are currently casting a spell that can generate Hot Streak! ( Fireball , Scorch , etc.).

You have Hot Streak! in hand before the cast completes.

You queue a Hot Streak! spender ( Pyroblast or Flamestrike ) as the cast completes.
 

Note: You can swap Scorch for Fireball and other spells that Hot Streak! .

Display Animated Double Pyroblast Example

So to reiterate on the most basic example: Begin casting Fireball , convert Heating Up into Hot Streak! with Fire Blast while casting (try doing it midway through the cast), then press Pyroblast as the Fireball finishes. If both Crit, press Pyroblast again. If this is still not working for you, know that you are not alone. It's so common that we have devised a training method for you:

The timing of your spellcasts and travel-times as a Fire Mage is something you should familiarize yourself with, and the best way to understand Double Pyroblast is to see it yourself. Practicing Double Pyroblast achieves both goals! Find a Target Dummy that is above 90% health, spec Sunfury with Firestarter , unequip your gear, and repeat the following sequence:

Pre-cast Pyroblast (Do not repeat this step).
 
 Fireball 

 Fire Blast (if available) or Fireball 

Queue Pyroblast as the Fireball ends.

 Pyroblast again.

 Repeat from Step 1. 
 

The goal is to get to the point where you can repeat this sequence indefinitely, without mistakes. Add pieces of loot back one by one to bring your Haste back to normal levels. You can also cast Time Warp to increase the pace. Once you feel comfortable, you only need to add Combustion (Between Step 2 and 3) and you have it down!

Stop using Fire Blast charges and Pyroclasm buffs if Combustion will be up soon to ensure they are available during cooldowns.

Two simultaneous Flamestrike casts (one hard-cast, one instant with Hot Streak! ) will "munch" the proc and not result in a Hot Streak! . 

Hard-cast Flamestrike with Heating Up only then consume the generated Hot Streak! after. 

Avoid hard-casting Flamestrike with Pyroclasm with Hot Streak! already active.

The goal here is to proc Pyroclasm before the pull without entering combat.

You must activate Combustion in the last 150 milliseconds of the Pyroblast cast for this opener. 

Distance to the target is also a concern, avoid long travel times. 

 Only use this opener only if you are confident in your timing. 

If Fireball and the instant Pyroblast leave your hands at the same time, both crit. This means you get Hot Streak! for another Pyroblast . 

If Frostfire Bolt and the instant Pyroblast leave your hands at the same time, both crit. This means you get Hot Streak! for another Pyroblast . 

Execute refers to <=30% health. This is the range where Scald becomes active.

Above 90% ( Firestarter ), Fireball and Pyroblast will always Critically Strike. This means you can anticipate Heating Up . 

If you just cast Pyroblast (without Fireball ), and only one spell is in flight, you can alternate between Fire Blast and Pyroblast .

Do this until you run out of Fire Blast , or the target reaches 90% health.

 Pyroblast is instant and will always Critically Strike during Hyperthermia . 

Below 30% health ( Scald ), Scorch will always Critically Strike. 

Flip the logic and use Fire Blast to generate Heating Up while casting Scorch . Follow up with Pyroblast (since Scorch is guaranteed to Crit).

In execute, try and play close to the target so you can react quickly when your Pyroblast s Crit. Converting these Heating Up to Hot Streak! before beginning a Scorch makes you waste less Crits.

During filler, secure the Hot Streak! and queue your instant Pyroblast as a Fireball ends. If two spells hit at the same time, there is a grace period for counting crits.

 Flamestrike is instant and will always Critically Strike during Hyperthermia .

If Scorch and the instant Pyroblast leave your hands at the same time, Scorch Crits instantly and Pyroblast also Crits after a short travel time. This means you get Hot Streak! for another Pyroblast .

Two spells in flight that are guaranteed to Crit will always result in Hot Streak! . 

 Heat Shimmer makes Scorch instant. 

Since Scorch has no travel time, this crit can easily be wasted if you queue it from a Fireball . Only use this proc after spending on Pyroblast or Flamestrike .

 Flamestrike can be used at 3+ targets if you just want the max damage. Pyroblast is still worth using sometimes, even at a loss in AoE (due to priority damage).
 
As a compromise between AoE and Priority damage, Flamestrike in Combustion at 4+ targets. 

 Flamestrike outside of Combustion at 4+ targets. 

 Never Flamestrike during Firestarter . Pyroblast is better above 90% because Pyroblast is guaranteed to Crit.

Comment by Baleful 
If I'm not mistaken, there's something absolutely crucial missing from this guide.

Outside of combustion, when Heating Up is generated, you still cast another fireball. You (almost) never do anything else. On each fireball, IF the previous was a crit, then you Fireblast in the middle of your fireball cast and then instant-cast Pyroblast immediately at the end of your Fireball cast. If I was a new mage reading this I would read your rotation guide as "if you proc Heating Up, immediately cast Fireblast and then Pyroblast.", which is wrong.
